and the condition:

$$

$$
f(\ln(\log_5(2)))

### Step 1: Simplify the input to $ f(\ln(\log_5(2))) $

Let’s compute $ \log_5(2) $ first.

$$
\log_5(2) = \frac{\ln(2)}{\ln(5)}
$$

Then:

$$
\ln(\log_5(2)) = \ln\left(\frac{\ln(2)}{\ln(5)}\right) = \ln(\ln(2)) - \ln(\ln(5))
$$

So the input to $ f $ is:

$$
\ln(\log_5(2)) = \ln(\ln(2)) - \ln(\ln(5))
$$

Now, let’s compute $ f(\ln(\log_5(2))) $.

$$
f(\ln(\log_2(5))) = 5
$$

$$
\log_2(5) = \frac{\ln(5)}{\ln(2)}
$$

Then:

$$
\ln(\log_2(5)) = \ln\left(\frac{\ln(5)}{\ln(2)}\right) = \ln(\ln(5)) - \ln(\ln(2))
$$

So:

$$
f(\ln(\log_2(5))) = f\left(\ln(\ln(5)) - \ln(\ln(2))\right) = 5
$$

$$
f(\ln(\log_5(2))) = f\left(\ln(\ln(2)) - \ln(\ln(5))\right)
$$

$$
A = \ln(\ln(2)), \quad B = \ln(\ln(5))
\Rightarrow f(\ln(\log_5(2))) = f(A - B) = 5
$$",
